chunks.text: business objective: Customers currently have to call support to freeze a lost card or change spending limits. Build a secure self-service feature so they can manage cards instantly and reduce fraud risk. users and roles: customer and employee workflow and outcomes: A cardholder makes a purchase. The system checks card status, available funds, spending limits, and fraud risk, then approves or declines it. The customer and merchant receive the result. exceptions: Decline transactions with missing or invalid details and explain how to fix them. Flag suspected fraud for review. Support handles customer issues; fraud analysts investigate alerts.

Only authorized staff may override a decision, with the action recorded. business rules: no idea data and integrations: Collect the cardholder ID, card token, merchant, amount, and transaction status. The system connects to the bank, card network, fraud checks, and notification service. If a connection fails, pause or decline the transaction safely, notify the customer, and retry without creating duplicate charges. security and compliance: no idea service levels and scale: As a starting target, support 100 transactions per minute at peak, respond within 2 seconds, and maintain 99.9% availability. Recover within 1 hour, with no lost or duplicated transactions.

delivery constraints: Deliver an MVP in 12 weeks with a small team and existing bank/payment APIs. Keep costs low, meet with the product owner weekly, and review compliance requirements monthly. Plan for policy changes and release features in phases. validation and rollout: no idea

options.name: Agile
options.suitability: Best for frequent feedback and evolving requirements, with planned governance for high-risk work.

options.name: Spiral
options.suitability: Best when risk analysis, prototypes, and repeated risk-reduction cycles are central.

options.name: Prototyping
options.suitability: Best for validating uncertain user needs, workflows, and interfaces before committing to a full build.

options.name: Incremental
options.suitability: Best when value can be divided into validated, independently testable increments.

options.name: RAD
options.suitability: Best for time-boxed delivery with available users and modular, lower-risk scope.

options.name: V-Shape
options.suitability: Best when each specification stage needs a linked verification and validation activity.

options.name: Waterfall
options.suitability: Best when requirements are stable, fully specified, and changes are controlled.
